title: Karachi / Delhi
hook: 1900 → 1960. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Karachi / Delhi in 1900 and 1960, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1900 and 1960; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Karachi area anchor: 67.01, 24.86 (0 km from the nominal location); Delhi area anchor: 77.21, 28.61 (0 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1900 and 1960 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["British Raj"],["British Raj"]],[["Pakistan"],["India"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1900.geojson (SHA-256 9c9221c851eaba4948e11b2a0b078e89239231f8c74df0dc321750ae234f10b5); GeoJSON features [[162],[162]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1960.geojson (SHA-256 6067386755f8fc120a4fca44f198952a18da89cd062aa8013d5a0d08cbad8988); GeoJSON features [[134],[135]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1900 has same label and 1960 has different labels. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1900.geojson (SHA-256 9c9221c851eaba4948e11b2a0b078e89239231f8c74df0dc321750ae234f10b5); GeoJSON features [[162],[162]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1960.geojson (SHA-256 6067386755f8fc120a4fca44f198952a18da89cd062aa8013d5a0d08cbad8988); GeoJSON features [[134],[135]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: A historical reconstruction assigns a region a label. Does that settle a present-day territorial claim? Answer: No; this reconstruction does not decide present-day claims A dataset's historical classification does not adjudicate present-day sovereignty or rights.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[8]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: A historical reconstruction assigns a region a label. Does that settle a present-day territorial claim?
options: No; this reconstruction does not decide present-day claims
recall.why: A dataset's historical classification does not adjudicate present-day sovereignty or rights.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
